pr_comments: I'm realizing now I misunderstood the contract, and the implementation needs to be much more complex, to handle cases where more input is provided than can fit into the output space provided... I was only encoding what would fit, but it appears the contract actually requires the remaining input data to be saved off for later.

Turns out the implementation doesn't need to be more complex as it can make simplifying assumptions about the inputs, ala what UniversalCryptoTransform does.  And since this never previously supported anything other than one input block that entirely fit into the output, this won't be a breaking change.  I'll fix up the input validation accordingly.

issue_context.title: ToBase64Transform wholly inadequate to live in the BCL
issue_context.body:
As can be seen in the code, it transforms chunks *per 3 bytes*.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/57bfe474518ab5b7cfe6bf7424a79ce3af9d6657/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography.Encoding/src/System/Security/Cryptography/Base64Transforms.cs#L37

This means it skips any and all simd paths in Base64.EncodeToUtf8, not to mention a gazillion calls to this transformer with tiny arrays to get the data encoded.

Benchmarking this against `Convert.ToBase64String` *for reference only, I really do want a stream* on a random 4k image results in more than an order of magnitude difference. So if `Convert.ToBase64String` can do it in 10ms, `ToBase64Transform` does it in say 120ms.

review_comments:
Remember to submit doc updates: https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.tobase64transform.cantransformmultipleblocks

(Seriously, I don't know why we doc things like "always returns `false` as an implementation detail." If it's an implementation detail and people shouldn't rely on it, we probably shouldn't doc it.)
Can't reach low enough:  TransformFinalBlock also needs to be updated to support multiple blocks.
Ah, ok.  This contract is... interesting.

>  This contract is... interesting.

Isn't it, though?

* TransformBlock: Transform one (or, if supported, many) block(s) but do no apply any padding/sealing.
* TransformFinalBlock: For AllowMultiple=false, should throw for more than a full block.  Otherwise, apply any padding needed to incomplete data, process blocks appropriately, and if there's any data sealing (spiritual equivalent to an XML closing tag), do that, too.

Historically, AES One-Shot was `aes.CreateEncryptor().TransformFinalBlock(data, data.Length);`, for all the people who knew that our symmetric encryption transforms all set AllowMultiple to true.

CryptoStream, of course, does things the other way.  Everything goes to TransformBlock except whatever was unaligned (possibly Array.Empty).
Maybe dispose the MemoryStream at the end or set the last ``leaveOpen`` to false?
I rarely dispose MemoryStreams, especially in tests, as MemoryStream.Dispose is a nop.
